items.title: Can mypy be told to forget previous type if it doesn't matter?
items.body:
It appears that mypy is complaining about a code block like this (greatly reduced from my actual code):

import dataclasses

@dataclasses.dataclass
class Type1:
    fielda: int
    
@dataclasses.dataclass
class Type2:
    fieldb: int
    
def gettype1() -> Type1:
    return Type1(10)
    
def gettype2() -> Type2:
    return Type2(20)
    
def callfunc(num: int) -> int:
    if num == 1:
        entry = gettype1()
        rc = entry.fielda
    else:
        entry = gettype2()
        rc = entry.fieldb
        
    return rc
    
callfunc(1)
callfunc(2)

The important bit is the callfunc() function. There are two independent pathways for extracting an integer from disparate types. However, mypy seems to lock the type in at the entry = gettype1() line in the if block, causing it to complain about the types when I assign it in the else block.

I've solved this in the interim by using entry1 and entry2 but it seems unnecessary since entry would only ever be the correct type (for the point of view of code execution).

It may be that this is a limitation of mypy in that it's not really "smart" enough to figure out code execution paths but instead simply assumes a line is executed if it occurs before another in the file.

Is there a way to tell mypy in the else block that it should forget about any preceding "type-lock" on the entry variable and treat it as if it were new.

As an aside, I'm aware that there's probably a better way to achieve this, but the code base is inherited (and large) and we're basically cleaning it up in stages (with addition of pylint/mypy/bandit being the early stages).

items.title: How to remove the last frame of the played video in LibVlcSharp
items.body:
After I play a video on Libvlcsharp and it reaches the End, the last Frame is kept displayed, and it only goes away if I play another video. Is there a way to remove it or set it to black color instead? I have tried to dispose of the media, but it doesn't change anything!

public partial class FirstViewModel : ViewModelBase
{
    private LibVLC MainLibVLC { get; set; }
    public MediaPlayer MainMediaPlayer { get; set; }
    [ObservableProperty] string movieUrl = "";

    public FirstViewModel()
    {
        MainLibVLC = new();
        this.MainMediaPlayer = new(MainLibVLC);
        this.MovieUrl = Path.Combine(Environment.CurrentDirectory, "sample.mp4");
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    public void Play()
    {
        var media = new Media(MainLibVLC, new Uri(this.MovieUrl));
        this.MainMediaPlayer.Play(media); 
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    public void Stop()
    {
        this.MainMediaPlayer.Stop();
    }

    [RelayCommand]
    public void ResetCurrentFrame()
    {
        // Reset the Current frame to be Black, 
        this.MainMediaPlayer.Stop();
        this.MainMediaPlayer.Media?.Dispose();

    }
}

items.title: Why does filtering by run state remove later temperature samples?
items.body:
I am using Apache IoTDB 2.0.8 tree model for a device running-temperature page. Temperature is sampled periodically, while status is only written when it changes. The business page needs "temperature points while the device is running". I first put status = 'RUNNING' directly in the query, but only the status-change row remained and the later temperature samples disappeared.

Reproduction data:

CREATE TIMESERIES root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01.temperature
WITH DATATYPE=DOUBLE, ENCODING=PLAIN;

CREATE TIMESERIES root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01.status
WITH DATATYPE=TEXT, ENCODING=PLAIN;

INSERT INTO root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01(timestamp, status)
VALUES (1746424800000, 'RUNNING');

INSERT INTO root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01(timestamp, temperature)
VALUES (1746425100000, 72.4);

INSERT INTO root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01(timestamp, temperature)
VALUES (1746425400000, 73.1);

Without the status predicate, the status point and temperature points are on different timestamps:

SELECT temperature, status
FROM root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01
WHERE time >= 1746424800000 AND time <= 1746425400000;

Time temperature status
1746424800000 null RUNNING
1746425100000 72.4 null
1746425400000 73.1 null

My original query was:

SELECT temperature, status
FROM root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01
WHERE time >= 1746424800000
AND time <= 1746425400000
AND status = 'RUNNING';

It returns only one row, and that row has no temperature:

Time temperature status
1746424800000 null RUNNING

I also tried adding FILL(previous):

SELECT temperature, status
FROM root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01
WHERE time >= 1746424800000
AND time <= 1746425400000
AND status = 'RUNNING'
FILL(previous);

The result is still only the status-change row. By contrast, if I do not filter by status in WHERE and only fill:

SELECT temperature, status
FROM root.stof_posts_tree.status_filter.line1.d01
WHERE time >= 1746424800000 AND time <= 1746425400000
FILL(previous);

Time temperature status
1746424800000 null RUNNING
1746425100000 72.4 RUNNING
1746425400000 73.1 RUNNING

My current understanding is that WHERE status = 'RUNNING' filters the raw timestamp-aligned rows first. The later FILL(previous) can only fill rows that remain; it cannot bring back temperature samples that were already removed by WHERE.

For this "status change points + periodic temperature points" pattern in tree model, do I have to first fill status forward into an aligned result and then filter by the filled status in an outer query or in the client? Is there a single IoTDB tree-model SQL form that can express "previous-fill status first, then filter temperature points by that filled status"?
